[2021-01-02 09:04] naph7777 : Podcast - Player growth theory checks out. Looked at a bunch of my players and the first round of the recent draft (50'ish players)... Almost all players are growing between 7.5-8 inches on their HS FR height. Outliers are a 6" and a 8.5" (no 6.5's, no 7's - the 6" was http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/71650) The vast majority of the growth happens in 3 years. Sometimes you get 0.5-1" on 1 side of those 3 years. Very occasionally you get them on both sides. The most common situation is either no extra growth or only 0.5" on 1 side of the 3 main years.

If you're winning via possession you want more possessions in the game. If you're winning via efficiency you want less.

[2021-06-02 13:58] naph7777 : If you have one established team, and you go all in on a player and you lose. There is the cost of rebuilding your only team after essentially missing a season of recruiting.   If you have just taken over a team (particularly a 2nd or subsequent team), and you go all in on a player and you lose.... So what? The team sucked anyway, and you're not invested in their success yet. You haven't really lost anything. You can either try again at essentially no cost... Or could sign up and get a 3rd, 4th whatever team, and just keep buying lotto tickets (going all in on high quality players) until you win one. Does that strategy scale in a way that is healthy for the game? There were only 32 5-star players in the game this season. There are way more than 32 bot teams that could sign up and attempt a "5* or bust" strategy with their recruiting.  As best I can tell the problem being alluded to is that this has happened before in this game. Where teams have tanked multiple seasons and shed all their scholarships intentionally so they could sign multiple 5* recruits in the same class, then attempt to build that way. I think that's why the LL5/6 recruiting penalty on 5* (and 4*) recruits got implemented. Having 1 or more teams pursuing that kind of strategy made the game less enjoyable for enough people that a change was made.

As talked about on the podcast, they don’t really mean anything other than with respect to potential redshirt decisions.  Anyway, I don’t know how to do pretty graphs like <@!453580403366821899> , so I just list the raw data below.  I only looked at seniors and there is not enough data to get exact numbers in all cases.  I did find a couple of things that I thought were interesting.  First, I looked at the events log during the flip to see the order and development #0 occurred prior to the star ranking, so we should be able to measure using current SI.  Also, I realize that I am going back a couple of podcasts, but I wanted to blow <@!275006169045794829> mind mind by pointing out that some players with the same SI have different star rankings.  For example, this 13 pot player with 108 SI is a 5 star: http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/107331
[2021-06-08 04:16] mainecougar : , while this 13 pot player with 108 SI is a 4 star http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/107615 Same is true of several 12 pot players with 109 SI, some are 3 stars while others are 4 stars.  Everyone above 109 was a 4 star and everyone below 109 was a 3 star, so it is clear that is the border. I recall that <@!94676029846593536> and others on the podcast have talked about how the numbers shown are rounded and I wonder if that is what is causing the confusion.  Perhaps someone whose true SI is 108.75 is shown as 109, but in order to be a 4 star, they have to be 109.00 or higher.  I don’t know, just a guess.  Anyway, the numbers: 13 pot 3 star- 95 or less 13 pot 4 star-95-108 13 pot 5 star- 108+  12 pot 3 star-109 or less 12 pot 4 star-109-(121 or 124) (there is a 121 4 star and 124 5 star so the line is somewhere around there, I note that <@!453580403366821899> had 124 in his graph so that is likely it) 12 pot 5 star-121/124+  There are no 11 pot 4 or 5 stars, so not sure where the line is.  Highest 3 star is 121. Hope this was helpful.

[2021-07-11 23:35] mainecougar : <@!453580403366821899> Here is an update on the star ranking system.  As pschwatz said, they appear to be every 5 development updates.  So recruiting #0 (development #0), recruiting #18 (development #5) and today was recruiting #35 (development #10).  If my math is correct, development #15 would be the last day of the season.  I’m not sure that the star ranking occurs that day (or if there is even an update).  I seem to recall that there was a star ranking update on development #14, which would be two weeks from today, but I could be mistaken.  As we have talked about before, it appears that the last star ranking update prior to the flip is what determines the star level that a player graduates with and not development #0 that occurs at the flip.  I think we also agree that star rankings aren’t of great value as they are simply the result of a mathematical formula (granted they do indicate higher SI and/or POT), other than with respect to redshirt penalties in recruiting.  Anyway, here is the data, unfortunately this is a small sample size, so not able to always get the exact SI that divides the star rankings.  As we have also discussed, sometimes players with the same POT and SI have different star rankings, indicating that the SI needed may go out to at least one decimal place or may not round up, unlike a player’s SI.  First number is for recruiting #18, second is for recruiting #35.  13 POT 5 star: 112+; 115+.  13 POT 4 star: 96-98+; 101+.  12 POT 5 star: 126-127+; 129-133+.  12 POT 4 star: 112/113+; 116+.  No 11 POT’s are ranked 4 star or 5 star.  Highest ranked 3 star was 123 and then 127, so 4 star is at least at those levels.  We may be able to know more next star ranking update, but it is possible that Steve is simply adding 3 SI each star ranking update.
